Union Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan today handed over the first installment
of three lakh houses worth Rs. 3,600 crore to Adhrapadesh under the Pradhan Mantri
Awasiyo Janakrami 2.0 at an event in Guntur district. Mr. Chahan also laid the foundation
stone for the country's first pilot housing project using 3D concrete printing technology
comprising 177 houses at a cost of 14 crore rupees. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu
Naidu was present on the occasion. Addressing the gathering, the Union Minister described
the 3D concrete printing project as a major step towards modernizing rural housing.
3D concrete printing technology.
We are going to build these houses using 3D concrete printing technology, a new technology
which will take less time as we are currently adopting this technology on an experimental
basis.
Our effort will be to ensure these houses are completed within six months with lower
costs, less labor required, and a longer life span so that they last for a longer time.

Campaigning ended today for by-elections to five assembly constituencies across Tamil
Ladu, Puducherry and West Bengal and one Lok Sabha constituency in Assam.
polling for the six seats will be held on Tuesday while counting of votes will
take place on Friday. The assembly constituencies going to polls are
Madran Takam and Tharapuram in Tamil Nadu, Thattan Chawadi in Puducherry and
Reginagar and Nandi Gram in West Bengal. In Assam voting will be held for Nagau
Luk Sabha constituency. The assembly seats fell vacant following the
resignation of the sitting legislators while the Nagau Luk Sabha seat
became awakened after the resignation of Congress leader Pradyut Bordaloy.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Sedeesh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues, guided
by this vision for Seva and Sushasan.
The government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Vixit Bharat
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming
lives.
Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated
into ease of justice through the new criminal laws.
These laws are the Bharatiya Nyae Sahita 2023, the Bharatiya Nagrik Surakshah Sahita 2023
and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhaniam 2023.
The new criminal laws which came into force from 1st of July 2024 mark a significant
step towards empowering the citizens.
These laws aim to create a more accessible, supportive and efficient justice system for everyone.
Under the new criminal laws, provisions such as introduction of zero FIR, fast-track investigations,
limited adjournments, forensic evidence collection and videography, gender-neutral offenses have been introduced.
Addressing a gathering after the implementation of new criminal laws,
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the core mantra of Bharatiya Nyaya Sahita is Citizen First.
In a major legal reform, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sahita 2023 has introduced stringent provisions
to tackle organized crime and enhance safety for women and children.
Talking exclusively to Akashwani News, Sunil Kumar, advocate in Delhi High Court, said
the new criminal laws introduced provisions for organized crimes, terrorism, mob lynching
and recognized digital evidences and promote electronic FIRs.
The three new criminal laws, Bharti Naya Sanghita, Bharti Nagarik Suraksha Sanghita and Bharti
Asakshath Inyam, replace the old IPC, CRPC and evidence act.
Their main advantages are modernization of criminal law, faster justice, greater use
of technology, and stronger protection for victims.
Earlier, different punishments were prescribed for gang rape on a girl below the age
of 16 years and 12 years.
The provision has been modified and now gang rape on a woman below the age
of 18 years is punishable with imprisonment of life or death.
Saklein Akhtar, Aakashwani News, Delhi.
Iran has said the Strait of Urmuz will not reopen until the United States meets seven
conditions outlined in a June interim agreement, as Tehran and Washington remain at odds over
efforts to end their conflict. Iranian state media today quoted parliament speaker Mohammad
Bakr Kalibaf as saying that Tehran's position on reopening the strategic waterway was
completely clear and firm.
Separately, Iranian Army spokesperson Mohamed Akarminiah said Iran will seek to extend the
range of its missiles following its recent war with the United States.
Speaking to a news agency, he said the conflict had highlighted the need for Iran to develop
longer-range missiles and that the country had already begun taking steps in that direction.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has claimed that the war with Iran will end very quickly
and predicted that oil prices will fall sharply once the conflict was over.
On the other hand, Yemeni forces have claimed that the Iran-Bat-Houthi group suffered heavy
losses on key fronts in Yemen, while Saudi Arabia has rejected a Houthi claim that Aramco
oil refinery in Riyadh was targeted in a missile and drone attack.
According to media reports, the Yemeni armed forces of the internationally recognized
government carried out 97 operation against Houthi reinforcements on the Tour
Al-Badha and Tezfrans. On to sports now. The curtain has come down on the Asian
Games with a dazzling closing ceremony at Aichi Nagoya in Japan bringing more
than two weeks of action-packed competition across 43 disciplines to
an end. The ceremony featured the traditional parade of athletes, the
lowering of the Asian Games flag and the formal handover of ceremonial
torch and flag to Doha, the host city for the 2030 edition. Proudly carrying the Indian
tri-colour for the closing ceremony was India's women's flag bearer and shooting star Neeraudhanda.
The double gold medalist led the Indian contingent in a proud movement for the nation. India
signed off from the Games in fourth place in the overall medal standings behind
China, Japan and South Korea. The Indian contingent returned with an impressive hall
of 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.
It is India's second highest medal tally in Asian Games history, surpassed only by the
record-breaking performance at Hangzhou in 2023.
As the Asian Games draw to close today, Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister
Narendra Modi extended compliments to every member of the Indian contingent for representing
the nation with determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit. In their messages,
the vice-president and the prime minister congratulated all the medal winners and expressed hope
that these games inspire even greater achievements in the years ahead and strengthen sports at the
grassroots too. The Indian Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and
south interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahi, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next two to three
days. The IMD said, Thunderstorm, accompanied with lightning and gusty winds, may prevail
over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand and Tripura tomorrow.
